The package contains clear malicious indicators: at import it base64-decodes a URL, fetches remote content from that URL, then base64-decodes, zlib-decompresses and exec()s the result. This is dynamic remote code execution and obfuscation (base64 + compression) used to evade static analysis and deliver arbitrary payloads (typical backdoor/malware behavior). Executing fetched code at import makes this unsafe and malicious by intent.

The package fetches a remote resource (URL hidden in base64), then base64-decodes, zlib-decompresses, and exec()s the fetched payload at import time. This is classic obfuscation + remote code execution (dynamic eval/exec of a concealed payload), which is deliberate malicious behavior and cannot be validated as benign. Executing downloaded, encoded code on import is highly suspicious and constitutes malware.

The package fetches a base64-encoded URL, downloads a base64-compressed payload from that remote host, decompresses it and immediately executes it with exec(), and the payload and transport are obfuscated. This is remote, dynamic code execution (RCE) with deliberate obfuscation and a silent except:pass, which is a common malware/backdoor pattern and allows arbitrary hidden code to run. Even if intended as an updater, the implementation is insecure and effectively enables arbitrary remote code execution.

This is deliberate obfuscation and dynamic remote code execution (fetched from a raw GitHub URL) with silent failure handling — a classic mechanism for delivering and running arbitrary/malicious payloads.
